summary: This is the unit test file for the new speak method: for each kind of robot pet it checks the low-battery message, the happy message, the neutral message, and that the pet's own name appears in whatever it says.

lines.text: The ellipsis stands for the setUp method and the earlier tests from the previous listing, which are unchanged; only the speak tests are new here. In your own file, keep that existing code and add these methods below it.

assertIn checks that one string appears somewhere inside another, so the test passes as long as the message mentions recharging. That is deliberate: asserting the exact sentence would break the moment you reword the message.
The happy and neutral tests set the battery well above the low-battery threshold, otherwise the low-battery message would win and the test would be checking the wrong branch.
This test leaves mood and battery at whatever setUp gave them, because the pet's name should show up in the message no matter which branch runs.

Each pet type gets its own test case class, since each one overrides speak with its own wording. The four classes are near-identical in shape, which is exactly what you want when comparing subclass behaviour.
The substring has to match character for character, including capital letters and the space, so a message reading "best day" would fail this test.
